results: 1. alien limb / limb levitation with the eyes closed: POSITIVE - aimless movements of the right side with the eyes closed, posterior-variant alien limb
2. cortical sensory testing (astereognosis, sensory inattention): sensory inattention and astereognosis on the right
3. ideomotor apraxia (imitation of meaningless gestures): apraxia to meaningless gestures
4. myoclonus or stimulus-sensitive jerks in the affected limb: myoclonic jerks in the right hand at rest
5. dystonic posturing of the hand or foot: dystonic posturing of the right fingers
6. MRI brain - cortical atrophy pattern: moderate global atrophy with MARKEDLY ASYMMETRICAL atrophy of the superior parietal lobules and posterior frontal lobes, left hemisphere worse
7. FDG-PET brain: hypometabolism in the same asymmetric distribution
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Corticobasal syndrome due to underlying 4R-tauopathy (corticobasal degeneration), presenting with the posterior-variant alien limb phenomenon.

Alternatives to consider:
1. Alzheimer's disease presenting with a corticobasal syndrome (AD-CBS), as AD pathology can rarely produce this clinical/radiological picture
2. Posterior cortical atrophy with parkinsonism features
3. Atypical presentation of dementia with Lewy bodies, though the parietal-predominant asymmetric atrophy makes this less likely
dx: Corticobasal syndrome due to underlying 4R-tauopathy (corticobasal degeneration), presenting with the posterior-variant alien limb phenomenon.
